# Testability & Acceptance Criteria Checklist: Deployment and Release Process

**Purpose**: Validate that the acceptance scenarios and success criteria are measurable,
unambiguous, and objectively verifiable before implementation.
**Created**: 2026-08-24
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Measurability of Success Criteria

- [ ] CHK001 Is SC-001's "0 manual patch steps" defined against an explicit build procedure so reproducibility is objectively checkable? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK002 Is "reproducible"/"equivalent artifact" (SC-001, FR-002) tied to a defined set of inputs (lockfile, Node version, source version) and an equivalence definition? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK003 Is the "within seconds" bound in SC-003 quantified with a concrete threshold so fail-fast timing is measurable? [Clarity, Spec §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK004 Is SC-003's "names the missing value" given a precise expectation (all missing keys vs the first) so it is objectively verifiable? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK005 Is the scan scope for SC-004 ("0 secrets in committed source or the artifact") defined (which locations are inspected) so the criterion is verifiable? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]

## Acceptance Scenario Quality

- [ ] CHK006 Do the US3 migration acceptance scenarios define an observable idempotency outcome (no change on an already-current schema)? [Measurability, Spec §US3]
- [ ] CHK007 Are the US4 health-check acceptance scenarios stated with exact status codes and conditions for healthy vs unhealthy? [Clarity, Spec §US4]
- [ ] CHK008 Is "known-good release" given a concrete, checkable definition so the US5 rollback acceptance scenario is verifiable? [Ambiguity, Spec §US5]
- [ ] CHK009 Are acceptance criteria defined for a migration failure halting the release with an observable non-zero/halt outcome? [Coverage, Spec §FR-007]

## Threshold & Metric Definition

- [ ] CHK010 Are health-check responsiveness expectations stated with a measurable bound, or is their absence acknowledged? [Gap, Non-Functional]
- [ ] CHK011 Is SC-006's healthy/unhealthy distinction expressed as objectively checkable conditions (DB reachable → 200; dependency down → 503)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK012 Is the release-to-source-version mapping (SC-007) defined as an observable artifact (embedded build id) so traceability is verifiable? [Measurability, Spec §SC-007]

## Scenario-Class Verifiability

- [ ] CHK013 Are acceptance criteria defined for the unhealthy path (dependency down → 503) as an objectively checkable condition? [Coverage, Spec §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK014 Are acceptance criteria defined for a missing required configuration value (fail-fast) with an observable outcome and exit behavior? [Coverage, Spec §FR-005]

## Documentation & Traceability

- [ ] CHK015 Is SC-002 ("no undocumented steps") given an objective completeness criterion for the runbook (build, config, migrate, deploy, verify, rollback)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK016 Does every success criterion (SC-001..SC-008) map to at least one functional requirement so acceptance is traceable? [Traceability]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Lens: Testability & acceptance criteria | Depth: Standard (PR review) | Audience: Reviewer
- Complements the broader `deployment.md` checklist (does not duplicate its completeness/consistency items)
